text_summary.body: Nebuchadnezzar's servants besieged Jerusalem; the king came; Jehoiachin with his mother, servants and officials surrendered in Nebuchadnezzar's eighth year; the Temple and palace treasures and Solomon's gold vessels were taken; ten thousand captives including craftsmen and smiths, the mighty men seven thousand and craftsmen one thousand.

setting.body: ABC 5: in year 7, in Kislev, the king of Akkad marched to Ḫatti, encamped against the city of Judah and on 2 Adar seized the city and captured the king; he appointed a king of his own choice and took heavy tribute to Babylon. 2 Adar of year 7 = 15/16 March 597 (Parker & Dubberstein).

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V7CG4KY46JV2S8Q4Y0W2QN
constraints.textual_assertion: he reigned in Jerusalem three months
assumptions: 2 Chr 36:9: three months and ten days.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V7CG4KY46JV2S8Q4Y0W2QN
constraints.textual_assertion: the king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of his reign
assumptions: Under non-accession counting the eighth year (Nisan 598 – Nisan 597) contains 2 Adar = March 597 (ABC 5 "year 7").

competing_reconstructions.label: "Eighth year" (2 Kgs 24:12) vs "seventh year" (ABC 5; Jer 52:28)
proponents: R. C. Young (2004): 2 Kings counts Nebuchadnezzar's years without an accession year
competing_reconstructions.summary: The same event, counted from Nebuchadnezzar's accession year (Kings) or from his first full year (chronicle; Jer 52:28).

competing_reconstructions.label: Numbers deported
competing_reconstructions.summary: The figures may count different groups (all captives; soldiers and craftsmen; adult males of Judah); none is confirmed externally.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik counts 597 as Nebuchadnezzar's second major strike, lists the 10,000 and 7,000 + 1,000 figures, and places Ezekiel among the captives.
